global.headline: The Fed raises rates for the first time in three years
summary: The Federal Open Market Committee voted unanimously, 12-0, to raise the federal funds target range by a quarter point to 3.75-4.00% — the first increase since 2023, after cuts running from September 2024 to December 2025. Inflation remains elevated, the statement said; Chair Kevin Warsh called it still "too high" and promised a "timelier return" to 2%, while playing down the funds rate in favour of shrinking the balance sheet. Projections show 16 of 18 officials expecting at least one more quarter-point rise this year, four expecting two.
The 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.041% before the decision, its highest since July 2007, and closed near 5.01%. Trump, who appointed Warsh expecting cuts, said rates "should be 1%, or less".
global.geopolitical: A central bank raising rates weeks before the midterms, against the explicit demand of the president who chose its chair, is the clearest test yet of whether Fed independence survives this administration.
global.socioeconomic: The inflation being tightened against is largely imported — war-driven energy costs. Rates cannot produce oil, so the burden falls on mortgage and business borrowers already paying 2007-era yields.

global.headline: Seven Republicans back ending the Iran war as damage photos leak
summary: The House passed a war powers resolution 220-204 to halt military action against Iran without congressional authorisation — the third such vote and the widest Republican defection yet. Seven joined every Democrat, Nancy Mace, Mariannette Miller-Meeks and Zach Nunn for the first time. The resolution has no force of law; the Senate blocked both earlier attempts.

Serving personnel anonymously passed CBS photographs of wrecked US installations in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait — an E-3 Sentry with its tail severed at Prince Sultan Air Base, gutted barracks and vehicles at Camps Buehring and Arifjan. The Pentagon's inspector general puts equipment losses at US$3.7 billion across nearly 60 aircraft. Araghchi met Wang Yi in Beijing. No new strikes; Brent near US$108.
global.geopolitical: Tehran can now read the war's American price in the president's own party. Three new defections and a Beijing welcome for Araghchi days before Xi visits Washington both point the same way: waiting is Iran's cheapest strategy.
global.socioeconomic: Roughly 58% of Americans oppose the war and 66% of likely voters call it very important to their congressional vote. The leaked photographs put a physical loss against the budget office's US$38 billion.

global.headline: Washington met the Houthis in Oman and left Riyadh to fight alone
summary: Reuters reported that US officials met a Houthi delegation at the American embassy in Muscat over the weekend, days after the group completed its sweep of Yemen's Red Sea coast. Oman convened it; the delegation included Mohammad Abdulsalam, who is under US sanctions. Trump said "the Houthis called us, and they don't want to fight with us"; Vance confirmed direct contact. Mohammed bin Salman's request for military help was refused last week.

Riyadh said its air defences destroyed a Houthi drone south of Mecca on Tuesday before it reached the holy city's airspace, calling it a "red line"; spokesman Yahya Saree denied the group launched it and called the account propaganda. Washington raised its Saudi travel advisory to Level 3.
global.geopolitical: The security guarantee the Gulf bought with basing rights has been priced: America will talk to the group attacking Saudi Arabia rather than fight it. Every state hosting US forces now has that answer on the record.
global.socioeconomic: Saudi crude already moves through neither Hormuz nor the shut East-West pipeline. A kingdom fighting without its protector, on a coastline the Houthis hold, keeps the war premium in every barrel and every freight rate.

global.headline: Brussels offers Canada associate membership and moves to bar under-13s online
summary: In her State of the Union address in Strasbourg, with Mark Carney seated as her guest, Ursula von der Leyen invited Canada to become the EU's first "associate member": "We will move from CETA to an alliance for the future," covering technology, critical raw materials, energy and defence. The status does not yet exist, its content is undefined, and several member governments were angry at not being consulted — creating it needs unanimity.

She also proposed a Kids Act: no social media under 13, no personal account under 15, guardian-controlled accounts from 13 to 15, mandatory safe design for under-18s, a one-hour daily cap, and a reversed burden of proof requiring platforms to prove they are safe for minors.
global.geopolitical: Brussels is offering a country in a tariff war with Washington a seat inside the bloc's economic perimeter. If it survives 27 capitals, associate membership becomes a template for every state seeking an alternative to American terms.
global.socioeconomic: Reversing the burden of proof is the costly part. Platforms would have to demonstrate child safety to sell in a 450-million market — a compliance standard that tends to be exported rather than kept regional.

global.headline: Fiji declares an HIV emergency with one in 60 adults infected
summary: Health Minister Atonio Lalabalavu declared a national HIV emergency on Tuesday. About one in 60 adults in the country of fewer than a million people is now estimated to be living with the virus, against one in 167 five years ago — a rise running against the global trend. There were 2,060 new diagnoses in 2025 and 117 HIV-related deaths, up from 25 in 2021.

The driver is injecting drug use: people who inject drugs accounted for roughly half of 2025's new cases where the transmission route was identified, as methamphetamine trafficked through the Pacific by cartels reached local communities. Fiji first declared an outbreak in January 2025 and expanded testing, which revealed the scale of the epidemic.
global.geopolitical: Fiji is a transit point on a Pacific methamphetamine route, not a destination market. The health emergency is the visible cost of trafficking corridors that no single island state has the maritime reach to police.
global.socioeconomic: HIV is treatable, so the binding constraint is lifetime antiretroviral supply for a growing cohort in a small health budget. Deaths quintupling since 2021 indicates diagnosis and treatment are still arriving late.

singapore.headline: Databricks and Anthropic both plant Asian bases in Singapore
summary: Databricks said it will invest more than S$445 million (US$350 million) in Singapore over three years, quadrupling its office into a 32,000 sq ft headquarters and doubling local headcount from 250 to more than 500. The site is its Asia-Pacific and Japan hub and will house training and collaboration facilities for customers and partners.

Anthropic said on the same day it will open a Singapore office in October, its fifth in the region after Tokyo, Bengaluru, Seoul and Sydney, hiring across AI, finance, marketing, sales and economic research under ASEAN general manager Dale Finlay. The firm's economic index ranks Singapore second of 121 markets for Claude usage relative to population, at 5.81 times the expected level.
singapore.geopolitical: Both firms are American and both chose Singapore as the regional seat rather than a larger neighbouring market — a vote for predictable rules over scale, at a moment when AI governance is splitting between Washington's and Beijing's camps.
singapore.socioeconomic: Roughly 250 new Databricks jobs are real but small. The larger effect is where enterprise AI deployment across the region gets specified, billed and supported — and that is now here.

singapore.headline: MOE will pilot smaller classes and redesigned teacher roles in six schools
summary: Education Minister Desmond Lee told the Schools Work Plan Seminar that from January 2027 the ministry will pilot flexible learning spaces, smaller classes where needed, and a reorganisation of teachers' work at three primary and three secondary schools: St Anthony's Canossian Primary, Woodgrove Primary, Zhangde Primary, Commonwealth Secondary, Deyi Secondary and Jurongville Secondary.

Lee was explicit that smaller classes do not by themselves lighten workload — teachers may simply take more classes — so the pilot pairs them with a broader redesign of teaching and feedback. The ministry will separately study letting teachers concentrate on two of three non-classroom duties: form teachership, co-curricular activities and committee work.
singapore.geopolitical: Not applicable — a domestic policy pilot with no external dimension.
singapore.socioeconomic: Smaller classes in a system at full teacher capacity means either more hires or more periods each. Making that arithmetic explicit, rather than promising both, is what separates this pilot from a decade of smaller-class advocacy.

singapore.headline: Wong tells firms workers cannot be an afterthought in transformation
summary: Opening the SkillsFuture Festival at the Lifelong Learning Institute — the first under the new Skills and Workforce Development Agency — PM Lawrence Wong said companies must plan for their workers alongside business transformation rather than treating them as an HR afterthought. The festival runs to 28 October with 140 events and about 450 job openings.

The refreshed SkillsFuture portal carries more than 200 AI courses, and those completing eligible ones can redeem six months' free access to one premium AI tool — ChatGPT Plus, Google AI Pro, Manus AI, Microsoft 365 Personal or Singtel AI Pass — one per person. SWDA also opened Connect by SWDA at Paya Lebar, an integrated careers and workforce-development centre for individuals and employers.
singapore.geopolitical: Not applicable — a domestic labour-market initiative.
singapore.socioeconomic: Subsidising tool access rather than only course fees is a bet that the barrier is habit, not tuition. Six months is long enough to build a work routine and short enough to leave the renewal cost with the user.

singapore.headline: Ex-HDB group director charged over 161 unauthorised database searches
summary: Tan Chew Ling, 58, a former group director of the Housing Board, faces one charge under the Computer Misuse Act of accessing HDB's housing management submissions database on 161 occasions on 27 and 28 April 2024 without authorisation, and a charge under the Official Secrets Act of retaining documents and information on seven flats. The flats are in Kim Keat, Pasir Ris, Dakota, Dawson Road, Bedok North, Tampines and Shunfu. She was first charged in August; a pre-trial conference is set for 20 October.
singapore.socioeconomic: It lands the week the Public Service Division is reviewing a working paper alleging officials bought homes near unannounced MRT stations. Both turn on the same asset: what public servants can see about property before anyone else.

singapore.headline: NParks makes its largest wildlife seizure since 2021
summary: NParks said simultaneous raids on 14 September at the homes of six people suspected of selling or keeping wildlife illegally recovered 101 specimens, its biggest single seizure since about 120 animals were taken in 2021. Axolotls, leopard geckos, tarantulas, pig-nosed turtles, armadillo girdled lizards, rosy boas and Mount Elliot leaf-tailed geckos were among them; several species are protected under CITES. Thirteen animals were found dead and one was euthanised. The rest are in mandatory quarantine, their sources unknown and disease risk to animals and humans unassessed, before any repatriation or transfer to zoos.
singapore.geopolitical: CITES-listed animals reaching Singapore homes means the trade is moving through, not just to, the country — which makes enforcement here a link in other states' conservation regimes.
singapore.socioeconomic: The animals were advertised on open online platforms, so detection is cheap and supply is not. Fourteen dead of 101 is the welfare cost of a trade whose enforcement burden falls on quarantine capacity the state must fund.

word.definition: Material reproduced and circulated privately because official channels suppress it.
word.etymology: Russian samizdat, "self-publishing", coined as a parody of Gosizdat, the Soviet state publishing house.
word.example: The wrecked Sentry at Prince Sultan Air Base reached the public as samizdat — photographed by serving personnel and passed anonymously to CBS.
